leaders.name: Rex D. Geveden
leaders.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2015 as chief operating officer before advancing to CEO in 2017. Previously spent eight years at Teledyne Technologies rising to executive vice president, and 17 years at NASA including service as the agency's chief operating officer overseeing a $16 billion portfolio. Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in physics from Murray State University.
leaders.why_they_matter: As CEO he is the person BWXT puts in front of analysts every quarter to talk backlog, capex and the BANR/Janus microreactor program, making his earnings-call remarks the most load-bearing public numbers in the sector.

sources.label: BWXT (investor site) — Rex Geveden management biography
sources.quote: Rex D. Geveden is president and chief executive officer of BWXT, a $3.2B nuclear technology and manufacturing company headquartered in Lynchburg, Virginia.

leaders.name: Katherine (Kate) Haggerty Kelly
leaders.title: President, BWXT Advanced Technologies
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2012 as a systems design engineer on a small modular reactor program; became advanced nuclear systems program manager, then director for space and emerging programs at Advanced Technologies from 2022 until her June 2025 promotion. Holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Notre Dame and is a recipient of the Women in Aerospace Initiative-Inspiration-Impact Award.
leaders.why_they_matter: She now runs the BWXT subsidiary (Advanced Technologies, LLC) that actually builds BANR and Project Pele, succeeding Joseph Miller who grew that unit's program content 10x and landed two federally funded prototype microreactor awards.

sources.label: BWXT — "BWXT Announces Leadership Changes" (June 16, 2025)
sources.quote: Katherine (Kate) Haggerty Kelly succeeds Miller as president of BWXT Advanced Technologies.

leaders.name: Joseph K. Miller
leaders.title: President, Government Operations (formerly President, BWXT Advanced Technologies, 2021-2025)
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2011 as an engineer, became program manager for advanced nuclear applications in 2017 and general manager of Advanced Technologies in 2020 before being named president of Advanced Technologies in 2021. Began his career in the U.S. Navy aboard the USS Norfolk; holds a master's in radiation health physics from Oregon State and a bachelor's in nuclear engineering from Thomas Edison State College.
leaders.why_they_matter: He led BWXT Advanced Technologies through the buildout that produced BANR and the two first-of-a-kind federally funded microreactor prototype contracts, the track record BWXT cites as evidence its microreactor unit can execute.

sources.label: BWXT — "BWXT Announces Leadership Changes" (June 16, 2025)
sources.quote: Under Miller's leadership, Advanced Technologies achieved 10x growth in program content and successfully contracted two federally funded first-of-a-kind prototype programs for advanced nuclear microreactors.

leaders.name: Jon Ball
leaders.title: President, eVinci Microreactor
leaders.background: Previously held a series of executive leadership roles at GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy, including Executive Vice President of Market Development and Executive Vice President of Advanced Nuclear, where he led small modular reactor commercialization and a sodium-cooled fast reactor partnership. Began his career at Westinghouse's Hanford site as a project manager; holds a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Pacific Lutheran University and a doctoral degree in chemistry from Penn State.
leaders.why_they_matter: He runs Westinghouse's standalone eVinci accelerator business, the commercial and Janus-facing counterpart to Rademacher's government-contracting role.

sources.label: Westinghouse Electric Company — "Westinghouse Announces New President of eVinci Microreactor Business" (June 5, 2023)
sources.quote: Westinghouse Electric Company has announced the appointment of Jon Ball as President, eVinci™ Microreactor, effective June 5, 2023.

leaders.name: Rich Rademacher
leaders.title: President, Westinghouse Government Services
leaders.background: Previously served as Vice President and Chief Corporate Development Officer at BWX Technologies, Inc. before moving to Westinghouse. Georgetown University graduate.
leaders.why_they_matter: He is Westinghouse's public voice on eVinci's defense wins, having delivered the on-record quotes for both the Army Janus selection and the Air Force Malmstrom AFB award.

sources.label: Westinghouse Electric Company — "Westinghouse eVinci Microreactor Selected for U.S. Army Janus Project"
sources.quote: Reliable energy is fundamental to mission assurance, operational readiness and national security.

leaders.name: Scott Forney
leaders.title: President, GA-EMS
leaders.background: Leads General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems overall, the division housing GA-TES nuclear work alongside GA-EMS's power, space and defense-systems businesses.
leaders.why_they_matter: As GA-EMS president he is the company's public spokesperson for the Janus award, positioning GA-TES on the firm's 70-year reactor-design and 68-reactors-deployed track record.

sources.label: General Atomics — "General Atomics Microreactor Selected for US Army Janus Program" (Aug 26, 2026)
sources.quote: General Atomics draws on more than 70 years of nuclear innovation and reactor expertise to deliver microreactor technologies

leaders.name: Christina Back, Ph.D.
leaders.title: Vice President, GA-EMS Nuclear Technologies and Materials
leaders.background: Leads GA-EMS's Nuclear Technologies and Materials group, which carries the GA-TES microreactor and General Atomics' legacy uranium-zirconium hydride (UZrH) fuel and TRIGA reactor work.
leaders.why_they_matter: She is the technical (not just corporate-communications) voice for GA-TES, the person GA-EMS puts forward to explain the reactor's passive-safety design choices to regulators and press.

sources.label: General Atomics — "General Atomics Microreactor Selected for US Army Janus Program" (Aug 26, 2026)
sources.quote: Passive safety and operational simplicity are fundamental to our Tactical Energy System design.
